title: Output size of a convolution (random numbers)
hints: Add the padding on both sides before subtracting the kernel size.
prompt: A square input has side {{H}}. A convolution uses kernel size {{k}}, stride {{s}}, padding {{p}} and dilation 1. Using $H_{out} = \lfloor (H + 2p - k)/s \rfloor + 1$, what is the output side length?

title: Trainable parameters of an MLP (random sizes)
hints: A linear layer has in·out weights plus out biases; ReLU has no parameters.
explanation:
First layer: {{n_in}}·{{h}} + {{h}} = {{n_in*h + h}}.

Second layer: {{h}}·{{n_out}} + {{n_out}} = {{h*n_out + n_out}}.

Total: {{n_in*h + h}} + {{h*n_out + n_out}} = {{n_in*h + h + h*n_out + n_out}}. ReLU adds nothing.
prompt:
An MLP is defined as:

`nn.Linear({{n_in}}, {{h}})`, ReLU, `nn.Linear({{h}}, {{n_out}})`

Both linear layers use a bias. Give the number of trainable parameters of each layer and in total.

title: One gradient-descent step (decimals)
hints: Move against the gradient: $w \leftarrow w - \eta g$.
prompt: A weight is $w = {{w}}$ with gradient $\partial L/\partial w = {{g}}$. SGD with learning rate $\eta = {{lr}}$ takes one step. What is the new weight? (Two decimals are enough.)

title: Choose the lines of a training step
hints: The optimizer owns two of the three calls.
explanation: Gradients accumulate in .grad across backward() calls, so they are cleared first, computed from the loss, and finally consumed by the optimizer.
prompt: Runs one mini-batch of training: forward pass, loss, gradient computation and parameter update.
template:
for X, y in loader:
    pred = model(X)
    loss = criterion(pred, y)
    <<BLANK:zero>>
    <<BLANK:back>>
    <<BLANK:step>>

distractors.why: zero_grad() takes no loss argument; it only resets gradients.
Tensors have no zero_grad method; the optimizer (or module) owns it.
There is no clear() on optimizers; the method is zero_grad().
step() applies the update; it does not clear gradients, so they would keep accumulating.
detach() returns a tensor cut from the graph; it does not reset any .grad.
This only builds a tensor of zeros and discards it; it does not touch the gradients.
Optimizers do not compute gradients; autograd does it from the loss tensor.
nn.Module has no backward(loss) method; call backward() on the loss tensor.
pred is not a scalar loss, so this raises an error (and is not the loss gradient anyway).
grad is an attribute holding a gradient, not a method that computes it.
Tensors have no step(); stepping belongs to the optimizer.
Tensors have no step(); the optimizer applies updates.
nn.Module has no step(); the optimizer holds the update rule.
There is no update(); step() reads the gradients already stored in .grad.
This clears the gradients instead of using them, so the weights never change.
This computes gradients but never updates the parameters; it was already called one line before.

title: Flatten feature maps before the classifier
explanation: The classifier needs one feature vector per image, so everything except the batch axis is merged.
prompt: Turns a batch of feature maps with shape (N, C, H, W) into a (N, C*H*W) matrix and feeds it to a linear classifier.

blanks.label: keep the batch axis, merge the rest

distractors.why: Without start_dim=1 this also merges the batch axis, giving a 1-D tensor of length N*C*H*W.
This puts the batch size on the wrong axis and scrambles which values belong to which image.
This swaps two axes but stays 4-D, so nn.Linear would not receive (N, C*H*W).
squeeze only drops size-1 axes; a (N, C, H, W) tensor stays 4-D.
This averages over channels, throwing information away and leaving (N, H, W).
This adds another axis, making the tensor 5-D.
